newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian ports need $14 bln investment, official say.
newsitem.headline: Indian ports need $14 bln investment, official say.

text.p: Indian ports need 500 billion rupees ($14 billion) to be invested in the next 15 years to set up facilities to handle anticipated cargo traffic of 850 million tonnes by year 2002, a top government official said on Tuesday.
Yogendra Narain, chairman of the state-run National Highways Authority of India, said half the projected investment would come from state agencies and the rest from the private sector.

"The capacity in our major ports is already overstretched and these capacity constraints have resulted in heavy congestion, high berth occupancy, pre-berthing delays and poor maintenance," Narain told a conference on infrastructure.

"If this trend persists and our economy continues to develop at the rate of 6.0-7.0 percent, the cost of additional capacity to cater to the traffic needs of ports in the next five years will be over 120 billion rupees," he said.
Narain said an independent regulatory authority would soon be set up to fix and revise port tariffs.
He cited an estimate made by the Asian Development Bank which said that Asian countries would need about $1.0 trillion for investment in infrastructure.
Increasing private sector participation is required to support governments which would have to play a major role in port development, Narain said.
An expert group on the commercialisation of infrastructure estimated the requirements of investment in the next five years 1997/2002 at $115-$130 billion, he said.
The group had said the bulk of the capital would have to come from domestic sources and 15 percent from overseas, Narain said.

India recently announced a policy framework for attracting private investment to create new capacities in 11 major ports across the country. Indian ports are expected to handle up to 474 million tonnes of cargo in 2001/02 against 215.26 million in 1995/96 (April-March).
While expansion, modernisation and improvement in productivity at ports could contribute 100 million tonnes, new ports could add another 200 million.
India's exports in 1995/96 grew at 21.3 percent and imports at 28.7 percent.
M. Srinivas, director of Krishnapatnam Port Development Project in southern state of Andhra Pradesh, estimated investment in infrastructure in the next five years at $137 billion.

He said the government had planned for an outlay of $80 billion in the next five years, leaving an opportunity for foreign investment institutions and the corporate sector to invest up to $57 billion. --Dev Varam, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
